# Benji Wise

> Benji Wise is a builder in Boston who directs AI models to write software and holds the taste himself — a practice he calls vibe-coding. He is a senior at Northeastern University studying business administration with a finance concentration and an environmental studies minor, and is open to work in 2026. His site, thebenari.com, is published under the name The BenAri.

His stated position: "Optimization is the easy half. People are the hard half. I work in the gap between the two."

Recent output, as stated on the site: ten systems vibe-coded in about eight weeks, 288 commits, three of them running 24/7 in production. The recurring techniques are multi-agent orchestration, pgvector RAG, MCP tool servers, and live-broker trading.

How he works, in his own framing: he starts with a conversation, not a spec — sitting with the people who will use the thing to find the problem they actually have, then shipping the smallest version that solves it. He won't build for problems nobody has, won't oversell what a tool can't do, and won't call something working before it's verified. His example of the last point: he built an AI trading strategy, ran the research, found no real edge, and rebuilt it from scratch.

## Pages

- [Benji Wise — portfolio](https://thebenari.com/): The landing page. Covers who he is, the three selected projects, and the approach section quoted above. The three projects are framed as "01 — Built to be used" (Benari), "02 — Tested to break" (the trading system, listed there as intelligence-office), and "03 — Worth watching" (a sales race board).
- [Benari — an AI chief of staff you text](https://thebenari.com/benari.html): Benari is an always-on personal and executive assistant you text. A stateless Claude brain reads one message and routes it to the right specialist — calendar, email, tasks, memory — each a domain sub-agent backed by its own MCP server, over a pgvector memory that recalls the right context. Adding a skill means adding a module, never a rewrite. Nothing irreversible happens without a confirmation: outbound messages are drafted and only send on an explicit YES. It runs 24/7; production runs on WhatsApp via Twilio. The page itself is an interactive recreation with scripted, fictional sample data.
- [Signal Desk — it traded its own worst ideas](https://thebenari.com/signal-desk.html): An autonomous trading system that screens candidates, sizes positions and places real orders on a live Robinhood account, unattended, with the broker reached over MCP. Its live record, 9 June to 31 July 2026: 37 trading days, −5.02% against the S&P 500's +1.35% (alpha −6.37%), max drawdown 8.79%, 15 completed round trips at a 40% win rate. The finding is in its own recommendation log: of 233 tracked picks, the 132 it chose to trade are down 24.7% held to date while the 101 it passed over are down 1.0%, and the picks it marked high conviction did worst of all at −31.3% — its confidence ran inversely to its results. Concentration explains it: 233 recommendations covered only 25 companies, and just 10 were ever traded. Stops are the reason the account lost 4.8% rather than 24.7%. Reconciling the app's own ledger against the broker exposed 12 discrepancies overstating losses by $47.61, so every published figure comes from the broker, not the app. Sample far too small to be a track record — one $1,500 personal account. Not investment advice. The system's source is a private repo.

## Optional

- [Sales race track](https://thebenari.com/race-board/index.html?demo=1): A retro leaderboard that turns a sales floor's targets into a race on the office TV. Every rep is a car, a pace line shows who is on track, and 100% sets off the checkered flag. Dependency-free, built to run all day on cheap TV hardware. The public demo runs on mock data with fictional names.
